summary: The patch sorts the components that SSTable.delete removes by lastModified, oldest first. It has two correctness problems. First, it leaves the bug in the ticket unfixed: SSTableTidier still deletes the Data component explicitly before it calls SSTable.delete, so the 'DATA first' ordering the ticket blames is unchanged on the main compaction path. Second, it replaces deleteWithConfirm with FileUtils.delete for every component. FileUtils.delete ignores failures, so a failed delete no longer throws, the tidier's retry path never runs, and the transaction log can be cleaned up while sstable files are left on disk.
tests_detail: not run: review-only lens; the spec reviewer owns test execution

findings.problem: The ticket's scenario is SSTableTidier deleting the Data file out of timestamp order after compaction. SSTableTidier.run still does `if (datafile.exists()) delete(datafile);` before it calls `SSTable.delete(desc, SSTable.discoverComponentsFor(desc))`. Data is therefore always deleted first, before the new sorted pass runs. If Data.db is the newest non-STATS component, a crash right after that delete still changes the on-disk max updateTime, and LogFile.verifyRecord still marks the REMOVE record as corrupt on restart. Reordering inside SSTable.delete does not reach the code path the ticket describes.
findings.fix: Delete every component in SSTableTidier in ascending lastModified order. Remove the explicit Data delete and let the ordered SSTable.delete handle all components, or apply the same ordering there. Keep the 'retry if Data cannot be deleted' behavior by making the ordered delete throw on failure. Add a LogTransactionTest case where Data.db has the newest mtime and the crash happens after the first delete.

findings.problem: Before this patch, every component except SUMMARY was deleted with FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError on failure. The patch uses FileUtils.delete(String) for all components. That method calls File.delete() and returns a boolean, and the caller ignores it. A failure caused by permissions, EIO or a read-only filesystem is now silent. SSTableTidier relies on the exception to add itself to failedDeletions and retry. Without it, the tidier treats the deletion as successful, calls parentRef.release(), and lets the transaction log be removed. Leftover component files are leaked without any error. Missing files also get lastModified()==0 and are skipped silently.
findings.fix: Keep the existing error semantics. Call FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for each component in the sorted order, keeping the old best-effort delete for SUMMARY only if that is intended. Alternatively, check the boolean result and throw FSWriteError when a file that exists cannot be deleted.
